findings.question: Q1
findings.evidence: MinMaxScaler.fit_transform is applied to the full descriptor+target dataframe before GridSearchCV/cross_val_score.
findings.impact: CV folds inherit preprocessing parameters estimated using validation-fold rows; reported validation is not fully leakage-safe.
findings.skill_rule: Fit preprocessing inside each training fold.

findings.question: Q1/Q2
findings.evidence: RandomForestRegressor is fit on all training rows and its feature_importances_ are used to print the top 20 descriptors.
findings.impact: If these Top20 are then reused in Q2 CV, Q2 validation has feature-selection leakage.
findings.skill_rule: When evaluating Q2, selector and regressor must be one nested-CV pipeline.

findings.question: Q2
findings.evidence: x_scaler.fit_transform(x_train) and y_scaler.fit_transform(y_train) occur before cross_val_score/GridSearchCV and before the later 80/20 holdout.
findings.skill_rule: Fit scaler inside CV/holdout training partition only.

findings.question: Q2
findings.evidence: Official-test descriptors are transformed with x_scaler.fit_transform(x_test), not x_scaler.transform(x_test).
findings.impact: Test coordinates are mapped with test-specific min/max while the saved model was trained in train-specific coordinates; predictions are not in the same feature space.
findings.skill_rule: Never refit train-fitted transforms on test.

findings.question: Q2
findings.evidence: n_estimators, max_depth, max_features, min_samples_leaf and min_samples_split are tuned in separate sequential sweeps.
findings.impact: Parameter interactions are not jointly optimized; the final combination is not established as globally best.
findings.skill_rule: Use a declared joint/random/Bayesian search or state the sequential-search limitation.

findings.question: Q2
findings.evidence: train_test_split(..., shuffle=False) is used without an explicit order/group rationale in the audited file.
findings.impact: Performance can depend on arbitrary file order.
findings.skill_rule: Use random/group/time split according to data-generating structure and document why.

findings.question: Q2
findings.evidence: MinMaxScaler is fit on the full X/y before the 80/20 split; subsequent tuning and holdout evaluation therefore use transforms estimated with holdout data.
findings.impact: Holdout estimate can be optimistic or otherwise contaminated.
findings.skill_rule: Split before fit or use a pipeline.

findings.question: Q3
findings.skill_rule: PCA must be fitted only on training folds.

findings.question: Q3
findings.evidence: The same 20% split is repeatedly evaluated while selecting n_components, kernel and C.
findings.impact: The nominal test split becomes a validation set; its best observed accuracy is selection-biased.

findings.question: Q3
findings.impact: Under label imbalance, model ranking can favor majority-class performance.
findings.skill_rule: Use balanced accuracy/MCC/PR-AUC and class-specific metrics.

findings.question: Q3
findings.evidence: precision_score(y_pred, test_y) and recall_score(y_pred, test_y) pass prediction as y_true.
findings.impact: Reported precision/recall semantics are wrong; in binary classification they effectively swap roles relative to the intended arguments.
findings.skill_rule: Metric APIs must be checked as metric(y_true, y_pred).

findings.question: Q3
findings.evidence: x_pca_pred = pca_model.fit(pred_x).transform(pred_x) refits PCA on the test descriptors.
findings.impact: The SVM receives components in a different PCA basis from the one used for training; final predictions are not comparable in feature space.
findings.skill_rule: Use pca_model.transform(test) from the train-fitted PCA.

findings.question: Q3
findings.evidence: For a 'hERG/HOB - special' block, test rows are vertically duplicated before refitting PCA, then predictions are truncated back to half.
findings.impact: This does not repair the train/test PCA-basis mismatch and lacks a statistical justification in the audited code.
findings.skill_rule: Do not use data duplication to satisfy transform fitting requirements on test.

findings.question: Q3
findings.evidence: For each candidate n_components, PCA is fit on all rows before the 80/20 split.

findings.question: Q3
findings.evidence: n_components from 20 to 49 are compared by model.evaluate on the same held-out 20%.
findings.impact: The held-out set is used for model selection and is no longer an unbiased test.
findings.skill_rule: Use validation/nested CV and reserve final test.

findings.question: Q4
findings.evidence: t4.py consumes a prebuilt column named ADMET from data_all_train.csv, but the audited repository search did not reveal how that composite label was constructed.
findings.impact: Cannot verify whether favorable directions, CYP3A4 ambiguity, and the 'at least 3 favorable properties' rule were implemented correctly.
findings.skill_rule: Composite target derivation must be explicit and reproducible.

findings.question: Q4
findings.evidence: The code filters observed samples by pIC50 > 9, applies IsolationForest, then reports min/max ranges of selected descriptors.
findings.impact: Unlike unconstrained continuous optimization, the reported ranges are anchored to observed molecules; this is a useful feasibility-oriented idea, although the ADMET composite remains unresolved.
findings.skill_rule: Prefer observed/manifold-supported feasibility when direct molecular design is unavailable.

findings.question: Q2
findings.evidence: IC50 is computed as 10^(9-pIC50), consistent with IC50 in nM.
findings.impact: Target back-transformation is internally consistent with the stated nM convention.

summary.overall: The repository is valuable as a real learning artifact, but its validation/test transformation chain contains issues serious enough that numerical results should not be treated as independently verified.
